open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input
open_points.text: “module:surface turns every JSON text a request carries ... into its canonical form with canonical_values.canonical_bytes” but the operation takes “One JSON value” and must refuse “a duplicate key”
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text/bytes that still preserve duplicate members, or an already parsed value from which duplicate keys may have been lost?
options: Receive raw JSON text or bytes and parse it with duplicate detection
Receive a duplicate-preserving parsed representation
Require surface's parser to reject duplicates before calling canonical_bytes
open_points.default_guess: Receive raw JSON bytes and perform duplicate-detecting parsing inside canonical_values.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile identity
open_points.text: M22 says “Substitution: equal facts are the same spooled file”, while State 5 says “A SpooledFile is named by its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey)” and read_spooled_file “names it by its identity” without digest, size, media type or disclosure class
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile's identity all M22 meaning facts or only (run, producer node, map index, attempt, port, list index)?
options: All M22 facts form the identity
Producing position alone forms the identity
Producing position is a lookup key distinct from the value identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat producing position as the unique lookup identity and treat digest, size, media type and class as attributes.

open_points.subject: refusal reasons
open_points.text: “refuses with one code of the closed set below and a bounded reason naming the first failing check in its rule's order”
open_points.question: What exact, stable reason values and associated fields may accompany each refusal code?
options: A closed enumeration of check identifiers
Free-form human-readable text
A stable check identifier plus bounded contextual fields
open_points.default_guess: Return a stable check identifier plus bounded contextual fields.

open_points.subject: HTTP failure_detail
open_points.text: “at most failure_detail_bytes_max of it is kept as failure_detail” and send_prepared_request returns “a bounded failure_detail”
open_points.question: For an arbitrary, possibly non-UTF-8 error-response body, which bytes are retained and how are they represented as failure_detail?
options: Leading bytes decoded with UTF-8 replacement
Leading valid UTF-8 prefix only
Base64-encoded leading bytes
No body detail unless it is valid UTF-8
open_points.default_guess: Keep the leading bytes, decode with UTF-8 replacement, then cut at a UTF-8 character boundary.

open_points.subject: sandbox failure_detail
open_points.text: “only for the exception type and message” and sandbox.execute_function returns “a bounded failure_detail otherwise”
open_points.question: What exact failure_detail is returned for syntax errors, load failures, abnormal exits, limit failures and exceptions, including formatting and truncation order?
options: A fixed structured pair of exception type and message
A stable formatted text string
Outcome-specific fixed detail codes with optional message
open_points.default_guess: Use an outcome-specific stable detail code and an optional bounded exception type/message.

open_points.subject: store.open_store bootstrap
open_points.text: “Take the exclusive lock, check the data directory and remove temporary files before any record is read”
open_points.question: What happens on first start when the data directory, SQLite database, content area or spool layout does not yet exist, or when an existing database has an unknown schema version?
options: Create every missing path and initialize the database
Require the private data directory but create its internal store layout
Require the entire layout to be pre-created
Refuse unknown database versions or migrate them
open_points.default_guess: Require an existing private data directory, create its internal database and areas atomically, and refuse an unknown schema version.

open_points.subject: manifest_source revision semantics
open_points.text: “Return the manifest location and revision fixed at start” and bindings read “<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json at the configured manifest_revision”
open_points.question: How does a binding operation obtain a file at manifest_revision from manifest_location?
options: Read the current filesystem tree and require it to attest that revision
Read the file directly from a local version-control object at that revision
Treat manifest_location as a revision-addressable snapshot store
Use revision only as metadata while reading the current file
open_points.default_guess: Read the file from a local version-control object at the exact configured revision.

open_points.subject: get_repair_view with no implementations
open_points.text: get_repair_view pages NodeExecutions “with a continuation token that also carries the implementation set of its first page”, but store.page_records permits an in-set filter only for “a non-empty set of values”
open_points.question: How is the NodeExecution page produced for a newly created slot that has no implementations?
options: Surface returns an empty page without calling page_records
page_records accepts an empty set for this operation
Use an always-false special filter
open_points.default_guess: Surface returns an empty page with no continuation token without calling page_records.

open_points.subject: functions.add_captured_trial_case errors
open_points.text: The operation reads an implementation and SpooledFiles through store.read_records, but its Errors section says only “refused naming the first failing check”, while the global convention says “a reference to no record is still unknown_reference”
open_points.question: How are a missing implementation, source execution, StoredValue or SpooledFile classified by add_captured_trial_case?
options: unknown_reference for every missing named record
internal_error because trusted runs supplied inconsistent facts
refused as a failed capture check
Different classifications for request-named and trace-derived references
open_points.default_guess: Use unknown_reference for the request-named contract or execution, and internal_error for a trace-derived reference that should exist.

open_points.subject: rollback eligibility
open_points.text: “Activate an earlier implementation admitted over the current corpus” while the enforced checks only require “an implementation of its current contract version” with an admitted verdict
open_points.question: What makes an implementation “earlier”: submission order, prior activation, position before the current implementation, or merely being a non-current admitted implementation?
options: Any admitted implementation of the current contract version
Only an implementation submitted before the current one
Only an implementation that was activated previously
Only an implementation whose last activation precedes the current activation
open_points.default_guess: Allow any implementation of the current contract version admitted over the current corpus, including the current one as the documented no-op.

open_points.subject: effects.operation_element_conclusion attempt selection
open_points.text: “Read from the NodeExecution and EffectAttempt together”
open_points.question: When an element has several NodeExecutions and EffectAttempts after one or more not_applied resolutions and resends, which records determine its current conclusion?
options: The greatest attempt_number only
The latest NodeExecution in store order plus its same-number EffectAttempt
Fold every attempt through an explicitly defined state machine
open_points.default_guess: Use the greatest attempt_number and pair that NodeExecution with the EffectAttempt of the same number, while separately considering a requested approval for the next number.

open_points.subject: authored trial expected_outputs
open_points.text: “optional expected outputs” and “expected_outputs: StoredValues by output port ... absent when only the absence of failure is required”
open_points.question: When expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every contract output port, or may it specify only a subset to compare?
options: Exactly all output ports
Any non-empty subset of output ports
Each output is independently optional
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all output ports when expected_outputs is present.

open_points.subject: unrecorded spooled files and spool_run_bytes_max
open_points.text: A failed change may leave “a published file no record names, which nothing reads and which is replaced at its position”, while spool_file checks “the run's spooled files plus this one” against spool_run_bytes_max
open_points.question: Do published but record-less files count toward the run spool ceiling before they are replaced or the run spool is removed?
options: Count every published byte physically present in the run spool
Count only files named by SpooledFile records
Exclude only a record-less file at the exact position being replaced
open_points.default_guess: Count all published spool bytes, subtracting a record-less file at the exact position being replaced.
